result.strongest_objection: The entire fix to round-1's tautology objection (F1) hinges on a 'discriminating fixture' for TestWorkbenchGradeCompilerVersionDerivationsAgree, invoked repeatedly (AC3, M2, M3, M11) as the load-bearing proof that the daemon-side and producer-side CompilerVersion derivations can actually diverge and that the test would catch it — but the fixture's content is never specified, and no V-row demonstrates that the two derivation paths (archived verbatim string vs. TrimRight+SplitN) ever produce different output for any realistic --version string. V38-V41 only establish that TrimSpace is absent from host/archive and that current real binaries happen to produce identical results under both rules; none show a concrete input (e.g., trailing whitespace/CR, embedded blank line) where the rules diverge. Without that, the claim 'the real gap is FIXED, not just documented' is itself an asserted, unverified premise about the one test meant to close the quorum's most serious finding.
result.catch: Define the actual bytes of the 'discriminating fixture' referenced in M2/M3/AC3/M11 (what --version output triggers divergence between the daemon's raw-verbatim-manifest path and TrimSpace-style normalization), and add a Verification Log row showing the two derivations computed over that exact fixture produce different strings — otherwise the cross-check test may vacuously agree on every input exercised, silently failing to guard against the exact drift F1 flagged.
result.proposed_fix: Add a new V-row (e.g. V43) that runs both derivation functions against a hand-specified fixture string containing trailing whitespace and a second line (e.g. "AILANG v0.41.0 \r\nbuild abc\n") and shows proofCompilerVersionLine(fixture) != strings.TrimSpace(fixture) (or equivalent), proving the fixture is actually discriminating; cite this fixture by exact bytes in M2's test description instead of the unspecified phrase 'the discriminating fixture.'
